scope: Final noncausal residual analysis after retained i32 matrix-address narrowing and causal-only maximum guard; matched unchanged CUTLASS4.7 reference. Profiles are diagnostic, final timing comes from separate three-round Nsight Systems runs.

method.instruction_count: Dynamic warp Instructions Executed summed across PCs; verified against raw smsp__inst_executed.sum.
method.samples: Stall counts normalized by all samples in each individual profile and by executions. No conversion of sample differences into time.
method.hmma: 128 static HMMA instructions grouped into first/steady QK/PV sets of32.
method.memory: SourceCounters memory metrics grouped by opcode, retaining reported ideal and excessive values. These do not establish physical latency per instruction.

conclusions: The final static noncausal kernel executes slightly fewer total instructions than the reference (-0.19%); its measured1.65% timing gap cannot be attributed to instruction-count excess alone.

Runtime noncausal has3.53% more dynamic instructions. The largest positive opcode deltas are IADD.64, LOP3.LUT, IMAD.WIDE.U32 and64-bit predicates. There are offsetting reductions, so positive deltas must not be summed as the net excess.

HMMA short-scoreboard observations remain low:6 samples static and0 runtime, versus208/165 reference. Final causal instruction encodings equal the previously profiled narrowed causal kernels, which had0 observed HMMA short-scoreboard samples; none of these observations proves zero actual stalls.

The clearest remaining memory-pipeline difference is the emitted copy form: Rust LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128.ZFILL versus reference LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.LTC128B.128. Both execute67584 copies with identical global theoretical sectors1081344, but reported shared copy wavefronts are540672 versus270336. Both equal their own reported ideal; excessive shared wavefronts are0. This is a copy-form/scheduling candidate, not evidence of bank conflicts or a measured2x copy latency.

MIO and barrier sample shares are higher in Rust while HMMA short-scoreboard shares remain low. This supports investigating copy/load issue grouping and barrier arrival timing. Barrier, wait and async-commit instruction counts match; no unnecessary barrier removal is justified by these data.

Epilogue memory-operation counts match:8192 scalar shared stores,2048 LDS.128 and2048 STG.E.128. Rust nevertheless executes101888/120832 epilogue instructions (static/runtime) versus65536/82944, mainly extra LOP3/LEA/shift/index work. Epilogue sampled shares are only1.52%/1.86% versus1.30%/1.50%, so it is a specific cleanup candidate rather than an established dominant bottleneck.

remaining_candidates.candidate: Proven full-atom copy specialization and copy/load scheduling
remaining_candidates.constraint: Any specialization must prove a complete valid source atom and preserve the generic partial-atom zero-fill contract. Do not drop ZFILL or barriers from sample evidence alone.
remaining_candidates.status: Unproven performance opportunity; requires isolated benchmark and correctness/sanitizer validation.

remaining_candidates.source: Runtime geometry, pointer indexing and staging address calculations.
remaining_candidates.constraint: Narrow only with a complete arithmetic/range proof; current matrix-load proof does not automatically cover global copy addresses.
remaining_candidates.status: Direct excess-instruction evidence; fraction of remaining time unknown.

remaining_candidates.source: WarpTile::store and final shared-to-global output indexing.
remaining_candidates.constraint: Preserve lane mapping, alignment, output guards and disjoint-store contract.
remaining_candidates.status: Extra index instructions observed, but small sample share; no demonstrated timing gain.

caveats: Single sampled launch per profile; stall distributions are stochastic.
Zero observed samples is not a guarantee of zero actual stalls.
A sampled consumer may be waiting on an earlier instruction; per-PC attribution is not necessarily the originating cause.
SourceCounters ideal-wavefront differences between instruction forms must not be interpreted as proportional hardware latency.
Normalized category deltas are not additive portions of the measured gap.
The analysis identifies specific residual differences; it does not explain all remaining measured time.

epilogue.method: Starts after the loop backedge following the last static HMMA; excludes repeated loop-tail instructions.
